done_when: Find the root cause of each (Forge not waiting for its processes to exit, or the test checking too early or on a reused id) and fix it at the cause; both tests pass on every OS in CI three runs in a row; no test is skipped or loosened to pass

findings.body: A zombie retains its PID and start time, so this comparison reports it as running after termination. The previous command comparison rejected its changed, defunct command. This affects actual cleanup: `_stop` at src/forge/codex.py:373-376 exhausts both polling periods, while the timeout path at lines 241-245 cannot reap its own driver until that cleanup returns. An unreaped lock owner also prevents doctor from recovering leftovers because `_take` at lines 408-410 treats it as active. Check process state and exclude zombies while preserving identity across exec. Add coverage before reaping: the new test calls `proc.wait()` before checking termination, so it misses this case. The [Linux wait contract](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/wait.2.html) distinguishes termination from reaping.
findings.title: Treat exited, unreaped processes as stopped

why: Main's CI is red on and off: tests/test_codex_record.py::test_6_nothing_left_running fails on macOS and Linux (_down(pid) is False right after the stop), and tests/test_codex_reader.py::test_10_the_cold_read_runs_on_the_other_family fails on Linux (forge doctor doesn't report stopping a crashed forge read's processes), so every pull request hits them
